The Newton-Raphson method of optimizing a multivariable function $f:{R}^{n}\to R$ is

$$
{x}_{n+1}={x}_{n}-[{H}_{f}({x}_{n})]^{-1}∇f({x}_{n}),
$$

where $H({x}_{n})$ and $∇f({x}_{n})$ are the Hessian and gradient of $f$, respectively, evaluated at ${x}_{n}.$

Equivalently, at each iteration, the above equation can be rewritten as

$$
{H}_{f}({x}_{n})({x}_{n+1}-{x}_{n})=-∇f({x}_{n}).
$$

In our case, the gradient is

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(3{x}^{2}y-2x{y}^{2}-3x+{y}^{2}) \\ \frac{∂}{∂y}(3{x}^{2}y-2x{y}^{2}-3x+{y}^{2})\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6xy-2{y}^{2}-3 \\ 3{x}^{2}-4xy+2y\end{aligned}],\end{aligned}
$$

and the Hessian is

$$
\begin{aligned}{H}_{f}(x) & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂}{∂x}(6xy-2{y}^{2}-3) & \frac{∂}{∂x}(3{x}^{2}-4xy+2y) \\ \frac{∂}{∂y}(6xy-2{y}^{2}-3) & \frac{∂}{∂y}(3{x}^{2}-4xy+2y)\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6y & 6x-4y \\ 6x-4y & -4x+2\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson system of equations is

$$
{[\begin{aligned}6y & 6x-4y \\ 6x-4y & -4x+2\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}({x}_{n+1}-{x}_{n})=-{[\begin{aligned}6xy-2{y}^{2}-3 \\ 3{x}^{2}-4xy+2y\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{n}}.
$$

Starting with ${x}_{0}=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}],$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{[\begin{aligned}6y & 6x-4y \\ 6x-4y & -4x+2\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}}({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =-{[\begin{aligned}6xy-2{y}^{2}-3 \\ 3{x}^{2}-4xy+2y\end{aligned}]}_{{x}_{0}} \\ [\begin{aligned}6(1) & 6(1)-4(1) \\ 6(1)-4(1) & -4(1)+2\end{aligned}]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =-[\begin{aligned}6(1)(1)-2(1)^{2}-3 \\ 3(1)^{2}-4(1)(1)+2(1)\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}6 & 2 \\ 2 & -2\end{aligned}]({x}_{1}-{x}_{0}) & =[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -1\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Solving this system of equations, we get $({x}_{1}-{x}_{0})=[\begin{aligned}-1/4 \\ 1/4\end{aligned}].$ Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ={x}_{0}+[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{4} \\ \frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}-\frac{1}{4} \\ \frac{1}{4}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0.75 \\ 1.25\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Equivalently, at each iteration, the above equation can be rewritten as

Hf(xn)(xn+1−xn)=−∇f(xn).

In our case, the gradient is

∇f(x)=[∂∂x(3x2y−2xy2−3x+y2)∂∂y(3x2y−2xy2−3x+y2)]=[6xy−2y2−33x2−4xy+2y],

and the Hessian is

Hf(x)=[∂∂x(6xy−2y2−3)∂∂x(3x2−4xy+2y)∂∂y(6xy−2y2−3)∂∂y(3x2−4xy+2y)]=[6y6x−4y6x−4y−4x+2].

Therefore, our Newton-Raphson system of equations is

[6y6x−4y6x−4y−4x+2]xn(xn+1−xn)=−[6xy−2y2−33x2−4xy+2y]xn.

Starting with x0=[11], we have

Solving this system of equations, we get (x1−x0)=[−1/41/4]. Hence,
